summary: At approximately twenty-five years of age, Muhammad ﷺ married Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, a respected and wealthy merchant of Makkah who was fifteen years his senior. The marriage was one of singular devotion and would prove the greatest personal support of his life.
narrative:
Khadijah bint Khuwaylid al-Asadiyyah al-Qurayshiyyah was among the most prominent figures in Makkah before and during the early period of Islam. A widow of noble lineage and considerable commercial wealth, she managed trade caravans and had employed numerous men to conduct business on her behalf. Her reputation for integrity and sound judgment was well established throughout the Hijaz.

Ibn Hisham records in his recension of Ibn Ishaq's Sirah that Khadijah hired Muhammad ﷺ to lead one of her trading expeditions to Syria, accompanied by her servant Maysarah. The journey proved successful beyond expectation. Maysarah returned with reports of the young man's exceptional honesty, his sound management of the trade, and several remarkable signs he had observed — including that a monk named Nestorius, observing him from afar, remarked that none but a prophet could have rested under that particular tree. Khadijah, already impressed by the reports she received, proposed marriage through an intermediary. Muhammad ﷺ accepted, and his uncle Abu Talib conducted the marriage ceremony.

Ibn Sa'd in his Tabaqat al-Kubra and al-Tabari in his Tarikh record that Khadijah was approximately forty years old at the time of the marriage, while the Prophet ﷺ was twenty-five. The marriage contract was conducted with a dowry of twenty young camels according to some narrations, with Abu Talib delivering the khutbah.

The union was monogamous throughout Khadijah's lifetime — the Prophet ﷺ took no other wives while she lived, a fact noted by classical scholars as evidence of deep mutual affection and loyalty. She bore him six children: two sons, al-Qasim and Abdullah (both of whom died in infancy), and four daughters: Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, and Fatimah.

When the first revelation descended on Hira fifteen years after their marriage, it was Khadijah who comforted the Prophet ﷺ, wrapping him in a garment and saying with certainty: 'By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You maintain family ties, speak truthfully, bear the burdens of others, earn for the destitute, honour your guests, and support the victims of calamity.' This account is recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (Book 1, Hadith 3) and constitutes among the most celebrated passages in the seerah literature.

Khadijah was the first person to accept Islam. Jibreel (upon him be peace) conveyed to the Prophet ﷺ that Allah sent His salaam to Khadijah and gave her glad tidings of a palace of pearl in Jannah, a narration recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (Book 73, Hadith 26) and Sahih Muslim. Ibn Kathir in al-Bidayah wal-Nihayah states that the Prophet ﷺ mourned her death deeply and that she died in Ramadan of the tenth year of his prophethood — the year known as the Year of Sorrow.
